title: Episode #001: Ionian Pre-Socratic Philosophy
note: The episode this lesson helps you remember. Logos is an unofficial companion and is not affiliated with the show.

title: Presocratic Philosophy
note: Overview of the early Greek thinkers. Their own writing survives mostly in fragments and later reports.

title: Thales of Miletus
note: What ancient reports say about Thales. Doubts remain whether he wrote anything at all.

title: Anaximander
note: Covers his cosmology and his account of how the first humans survived.

title: Anaximenes
note: Covers his view that air is the basic stuff of the world.

title: Heraclitus
note: Scholars still debate how far Heraclitus held a radical theory of flux and what he meant by logos.

title: Democritus
note: Covers his atomism and his split between sense experience and reasoned knowledge.

title: Leucippus
note: Ancient sources credit Leucippus with originating atomism. Little is known about his life.

title: Ancient Atomism
note: How atomism developed and how it answered earlier arguments about change and division.

title: Zeno's Paradoxes
note: Explains the halfway paradox and how later mathematics approaches it.

title: Monism
note: Monism comes in several forms. The lesson uses the simple, Aristotle-style sense: one basic kind of stuff.

title: Episode #003: Socrates and the Sophists
note: The episode this lesson helps you remember. Logos is an unofficial companion and is not affiliated with the show.

title: Socrates
note: Dates, the three main sources (Aristophanes, Xenophon, Plato), the Socratic problem, and the trial.

title: The Sophists
note: What the word meant, who the main sophists were, and why our picture is coloured by Plato.

title: Protagoras
note: The man-measure saying and how scholars read it. The relativist reading comes mainly from Plato.

title: Gorgias
note: His arrival in Athens in 427 BCE and his speech defending Helen.

title: Socrates
note: The Socratic problem, his method and his trial.

title: Protagoras
note: Dates and a short account of his thought, apart from general ideas of the sophists.

title: Sophists
note: Overview of who counted as a sophist and how they were seen.

title: Episode #002: Italian Pre-Socratic Philosophy
note: The episode this lesson helps you remember. Logos is an unofficial companion and is not affiliated with the show.

title: Pythagoras
note: Separates the early evidence about Pythagoras from later legend, including the blacksmith tale and the theorem.

title: Pythagoreanism
note: The later Pythagorean tradition, its mathematics and its disputed link to Orphism.

title: Parmenides
note: Reading of the poem, the two ways of inquiry and the debates over whether he denied all change.

title: Empedocles
note: Covers the four roots, Love and Strife and the doubtful biographical tales.

title: Parmenides
note: Dating dispute (about 540 or 515 BCE) and his use of deductive argument.

title: Empedocles
note: Life, the volcano legend, his four roots and his account of how species arose.
